title: Adaptive latency-aware retry profiles and idempotency coalescer
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement adaptive retry profiles that adjust backoff and retry windows based on observed endpoint latency and token-cost budgets, plus an 'idempotency coalescer' that safely collapses concurrent retry attempts for the same logical operation across SDK instances. Deliver cross-language reference implementations (Python/TS/Go), telemetry hooks, and migration guidance for existing idempotency flows.
acceptance_criteria: Endpoint-level adaptive retry presets available in SDKs with sane defaults for P95 latency, token-cost ceilings, and max retry budget
Idempotency coalescer implemented as an optional SDK middleware that prevents duplicate server-side side-effects for in-flight retries across processes (best-effort, documented semantics)
Comprehensive/unit and integration tests for stream resume behavior when id-key is present or absent
Telemetry emits retry decisions, backoff adjustments, coalescer hits/misses, and estimated cost impact
Docs and migration guide published with code samples for Python/TS/Go and a stable feature flag toggle
test_plan: Unit tests for backoff policy selection and id-key hashing; integration tests against a local test harness that simulates increased p95 latency and transient errors; canary rollout in staging with SDK telemetry validated against the console dashboard; fault-injection scenarios for streaming resume and duplicate suppression.
work_items: Spec: define signals (p95 latency, error rate, token-cost) and thresholds for profile shifts
Prototype: Python middleware for adaptive backoff selection and idempotency coalescer
Cross-lang port: TS and Go implementations with identical behavior and API ergonomics
Telemetry: add counters and trace annotations for decision points
Docs: migration guide, examples, and sample config for Dedicated/Private deployments
Rollout: feature flag, staged canary, and rollback plan
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Coalescer could suppress legitimate concurrent requests if idempotency keys collide. Mitigation: use a conservative TTL and high-entropy hashing; document best practices for id-key generation.
Risk: Adaptive profiles might oscillate under noisy telemetry. Mitigation: smoothing windows and hysteresis before profile changes; default to conservative presets for new tenants.
Risk: Cross-language semantics drift. Mitigation: canonical tests and a shared test harness executed in CI for all three SDKs.
change_log: 2026-02-20: Created ticket (Asha). Initial spec draft attached.
2026-02-27: Spike complete — Python prototype shows 18% token-cost reduction on synthetic workload (Marco).
2026-03-04: Design review with PM and security. Decided coalescer will be opt-in and documented as best-effort; KMS/HSM not required.
2026-03-09: PR opened for Python implementation; tests added for streaming resume cases. https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4817 (Marco)
2026-03-10: Updated acceptance criteria to include console telemetry dashboard requirements (Asha).
notes: Design trade-offs: We considered a single global retry policy but picked per-endpoint adaptive profiles to avoid cold-start oscillations across heterogeneous workloads.
Id-key format recommendation: 'tenant:operation:sha256(payload)' with max 128 bytes. Provide helper utilities to compute id-key across languages.
Operational playbook: If coalescer hit rate > 40% and user reports missing side-effects, disable coalescer and collect hashed payload samples for analysis.
SDK ergonomics: Expose a builder API that lets teams opt into 'conservative', 'balanced', or 'aggressive' adaptive modes. Default is 'balanced'.
